findings.reason: the section should name an evidence fragment (its own or §3's goldens.html) so the decision record survives and a later reader can open it.
findings.text: §7's done-when requires the harness to report the rerank-vs-fusion table, per-question wins/losses, the generic and role-aware questions side by side, and p95 wall time, yet names no durable path for any of it while §3 points at `docs/evidence/fragments/signal-search-finds-the-measured-signal/goldens.html` and §10 at `descriptions.html`; a node has no path to write to and may emit the section's evidence into a scratch run directory

findings.reason: the section must say the harness arm is pointed at the shipped signal state builder (or state that its measure is on a proxy) so the switch is decided on the mechanism that ships.
findings.text: §7 states the product's rerank "gets a signal state builder: name, description up to 1,200 characters, unit, data class and accessor", but the arms §7 relies on to decide the switch are the harness's own (`tests/llm/test_signal_search_goldens.py:267` `_rerank_arm`), which builds its state with the generic `_rerank_state` over `_signal_texts` (name + description + unit only, `:306`) — so the ship-on decision is measured on a candidate state that is not the one the product ships, and a role-aware rerank that clears the gate on the harness state may not clear it on the shipped state

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every §7 anchor resolves: `rerank_candidates`, `_RERANK_QUESTION`, the harness's kept role-aware question (`tests/llm/test_signal_search_goldens.py:56` `_ROLE_RERANK_LEVELS`), and the server switch at `imas_codex/llm/server.py:1882` `_rerank_dd_paths = not (self.read_only or self.dd_only)`, consumed at `:375`. No extensionless href in §7.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §7's measure is falsifiable: the switch ships on only if the role-aware rerank beats fusion alone on both mean nDCG@10 and grade-3 precision@5 with p95 ≤ 5 s and otherwise ships off, and the generic-question arm measured beside the role-aware one (which §1 shows loses to fusion on precision) is the comparison that can return a non-improvement.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §7's done-when requires the harness to report per-question wins and losses, the two questions beside each other, and p95 wall time, but names no durable evidence path, unlike §3 (`goldens.html`) and §10 (`descriptions.html`).
rubric_items.naming: pass — §7 introduces no plan label or ticket number into a symbol or comment. The plan-named env var `SSFMS_JEV_ARMS` and the "§7 names" comment in the landed harness are §3 artifacts already carried as a follow-on; §7's own text does not restate them.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7's ship-on decision is taken on a candidate state the product does not use, so the measured mechanism is not the shipped one (root-cause check passes: §1's table shows the rerank raised recall@30 and lowered precision@5 and its caption attributes the falls to ungraded candidates, matching §7; caller check passes: `_search_signals` is the named production caller).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §7's labelling node and scoring node both serve the one deliverable, the role-aware rerank and its switch, and §3 now assigns the two rerank arms to §7 explicitly ("§7 adds the two reranks").
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §7's followup ordering (§7 follows §4, §3 first) resolves, §8's third reader points at §7, and the code it names exists: `rerank_candidates` at `imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:171` is shared by docs (`:991`), code (`:1722`) and the DD-path search (`imas_codex/ids/slot_context.py:224`), and `_RERANK_QUESTION` is at `imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:84`.
